text_blocks.snippet: Oral and oropharyngeal cancers are cancerous growths that develop in the mouth (oral cavity) or the middle part of the throat (oropharynx). These cancers are often treatable, but early detection is crucial for a positive prognosis.
snippet_highlighted_words: cancerous growths that develop in the mouth (oral cavity) or the middle part of the throat (oropharynx)

list.title: Location:
list.snippet: The oral cavity includes the lips, inner cheeks, gums, tongue (front two-thirds), floor of the mouth, hard palate, and the area behind the wisdom teeth.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: A sore on the lip or in the mouth that doesn't heal, a persistent sore throat, difficulty swallowing or chewing, pain in the mouth, a lump or thickening in the cheek, pain in the ear, and changes in voice are potential signs.

list.title: Location:
list.snippet: The oropharynx is the middle part of the throat just behind the oral cavity. It includes the base of the tongue, the soft palate, the tonsils, and the side and back walls of the throat.
